newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asia share of world GDP forecast to beat U.S.
newsitem.headline: Asia share of world GDP forecast to beat U.S.

text.p: Asia's share of the world economy will overtake the United States by the year 2010, a Japanese government report forecast on Wednesday.
The report by an Economic Planning Agency panel said Asia, including Japan, would contribute 31 percent to the world's gross domestic product (GDP) by 2010, up from 26 percent in 1990.
It forecast that the U.S. share would fall to 24 percent from 27 percent while Europe's share would drop to 31 percent from 34 percent.
Japan's individual share is predicted to fall to 14 percent from 16 percent.

The report, entitled "Globalisation and the 21st Century," said it saw the world economy growing by a yearly average of around three percent through 2010 while trade would rise by 4.2 percent annually.

It said that growth of direct investment between developed countries, diversification of business across international borders, rapid growth among Asian countries and elimination of trade barriers were key reasons for world growth since the late 1980s.
The report warned that if Japan did not want to see its share of world growth drop below the 14 percent figure forecast for 2010, Tokyo needed to make improvements now in its economy.
The report said Japan was lagging behind the rest of world in riding the waves of globalisation, a shortcoming which had contributed to uncertainty about the nation's economic future.
It said Japan must reform through deregulation, efficiency in industry and improving the quality of its workforce.

Japan's government plans to address some of the shortcomings by the end of this month when it announces a package of sweeping deregulation in six major areas, including telecommunications and the financial sector.
